executive_summary.problem: Zoom's 140-person sales team is losing over 15,000 rep-hours per quarter to manual admin work across three disconnected tools, while outbound reply rates have fallen 50% year-over-year, threatening pipeline generation for H1 2027.
executive_summary.solution: A unified sales engagement platform that consolidates sequencing, conversation intelligence, and pipeline management into a single workflow, eliminating tool-switching and enabling AI-driven personalization at scale.
executive_summary.result: Based on customer benchmarks, Zoom can expect to recover 1.5-2 hours per rep per day, improve outbound reply rates by 40-60%, and gain real-time pipeline visibility that currently requires manual spreadsheet reconciliation.
executive_summary.investment: $85,000 annually, with a projected payback period of 3.2 months based on recovered selling time alone.
executive_summary.timeline_to_value: Core platform live within 6 weeks, full team rollout by week 10, aligned with your March SKO timeline.

output.their_situation:
Zoom's sales organization has grown rapidly over the past three years, and the tooling that worked for a 50-person team is straining under the weight of 140 reps across four segments. Today, reps start their morning in Outreach building sequences, switch to Gong to review call recordings, then toggle to spreadsheets to update pipeline numbers that their managers need for the weekly forecast.

This tool fragmentation isn't just an inconvenience—it's a measurable drag on performance. In our discovery conversations, Rachel's team estimated that reps spend an average of 3.2 hours per day on administrative tasks that don't directly involve selling. For a team of 140, that's 448 hours of lost selling time every single day.

The outbound motion has taken the hardest hit. Sequence reply rates have dropped from 12% to 6% over the past twelve months. Rachel's team attributes this to two factors: generic sequences that aren't personalized enough to cut through noise, and inconsistent follow-up because reps lose track of where prospects are across different tools.

Meanwhile, Zoom's sales leadership lacks real-time visibility into pipeline health. The current process involves managers manually collecting spreadsheet updates from their teams every Friday, consolidating them over the weekend, and presenting a pipeline snapshot on Monday that's already 72 hours stale. This makes mid-quarter course corrections nearly impossible.

Zoom has an SKO planned for March 2027 and wants to launch any new tooling ahead of that event to use SKO as the enablement moment rather than trying to train during a regular quarter.

executive_summary.problem: Walmart's data integration layer—a patchwork of legacy Informatica pipelines and custom Python scripts—is failing to keep pace with 14,000+ daily ETL jobs across four platforms. Data freshness SLA breaches have risen 340% year-over-year, and late-arriving merchandising data is costing an estimated $11.2M annually in suboptimal markdown decisions.
executive_summary.solution: A unified data integration platform that provides a single control plane across Walmart's hybrid environment, replacing manual pipeline management with automated orchestration, intelligent error handling, and real-time data freshness monitoring.

executive_summary.timeline_to_value: First production workloads migrated within 8 weeks, critical merchandising pipelines live within 14 weeks, full legacy migration within 6 months.

output.their_situation:
Walmart processes more retail data than nearly any organization on the planet. The data engineering team manages over 14,000 ETL jobs every day, moving data between on-premises Oracle databases, Azure Synapse, Snowflake, and Databricks. This hybrid architecture evolved organically over a decade, and the integration layer hasn't kept up.

Today, roughly half of those 14,000 jobs run on legacy Informatica pipelines that were originally designed for batch processing in an on-prem-only world. The other half are custom Python scripts written by individual engineers over the years—many poorly documented, some maintained by engineers who have since left the company. When something breaks at 2 AM, the on-call engineer often has to reverse-engineer the script before they can fix it.

The business impact is significant and growing. Data freshness SLA breaches have increased 340% year-over-year. When merchandising data arrives late, the pricing optimization algorithms that depend on it either run on stale data or don't run at all. David's team estimates this costs Walmart approximately $2.8 million per quarter in suboptimal markdown decisions—markdowns taken too late, or not taken at all because the data wasn't available in time.

Perhaps most concerning is the human cost. Walmart's 35 data engineers are spending roughly 60% of their time—21 FTEs worth of effort—on pipeline maintenance, firefighting, and manual error resolution. That's talent that should be building the next generation of analytics capabilities instead of babysitting legacy ETL jobs.

David's mandate from the CTO is clear: modernize the data integration layer, improve reliability to 99.5%+ SLA compliance, and free up engineering capacity for strategic projects—all without disrupting the 14,000 jobs that the business depends on every day.

input.discovery_notes: Canva's CS team of 22 CSMs manages 1,400 accounts across SMB and mid-market segments. Currently using Salesforce for CRM and a combination of Google Sheets and Slack alerts for health scoring. No automated renewal tracking—CSMs manually check contract dates. NRR has dipped from 118% to 109% over the past two quarters. Priya wants a system that surfaces at-risk accounts proactively and scales their high-touch model without adding headcount.

executive_summary.problem: Canva's 22-person CS team is managing 1,400 accounts with manual health scoring and no automated renewal tracking, contributing to a 9-point NRR decline from 118% to 109% over two quarters. At Canva's scale, each point of NRR represents significant ARR impact, and the current approach won't scale without proportional headcount growth.
executive_summary.solution: A customer success platform that replaces manual health scoring with automated, multi-signal health monitoring, provides proactive at-risk account alerts, and automates renewal tracking and expansion identification—enabling Canva's CS team to scale coverage without adding headcount.
executive_summary.result: Based on growth-stage SaaS benchmarks, Canva can expect to recover 4-6 points of NRR within two quarters, reduce time-to-intervention on at-risk accounts from weeks to hours, and increase CSM portfolio capacity by 30-40%.
executive_summary.investment: $35,000 annually—roughly the cost of 0.15 FTE on the CS team, replacing effort that currently consumes 3-4 FTEs worth of manual tracking and spreadsheet maintenance.
executive_summary.timeline_to_value: Health scores live within 3 weeks, renewal automation within 5 weeks, full rollout within 7 weeks.

output.their_situation:
Canva has built one of the most beloved design tools in the world, and their customer success team is a key reason why. Priya's 22 CSMs have maintained strong relationships with their 1,400 accounts, delivering the kind of high-touch experience that has driven Canva's impressive growth.

But the systems underneath that experience are held together with duct tape. Health scoring lives in a Google Sheet that three senior CSMs update weekly based on gut feel and whatever data they can pull from Salesforce. Renewal dates are tracked in another spreadsheet that someone started two years ago and has been manually maintained ever since. When a renewal is 60 days out, a Slack bot pings the assigned CSM—but only if someone remembered to update the spreadsheet with the correct date.

The cracks are starting to show. NRR has dropped from 118% to 109% over the past two quarters. In the post-mortem analysis, Priya's team found that 40% of churned accounts showed warning signs—declining product usage, support ticket spikes, or champion departures—weeks or months before they churned. But with no system to surface those signals, the CSMs didn't see them until the customer was already in cancellation conversations.

Priya's challenge is clear: she needs to scale the quality of Canva's customer success motion without proportionally scaling headcount. At a 64:1 account-to-CSM ratio, her team is already stretched. Adding more accounts per rep without better tooling will accelerate the NRR decline. But hiring more CSMs at Canva's growth stage isn't in the budget.

The answer has to be leverage—better data, smarter automation, and proactive signals that help CSMs focus their limited time on the accounts that need attention most.
